scope: all hypothetical R(4,6,36) graphs with exactly 220 edges and exactly three degree-11 vertices

proof_components.A1_nonincident_low_edges: degree-2 A vertex would be global degree 12 and require a triangle-free 9-vertex B-neighborhood; none exists
proof_components.A1_incident_low_edges: both low rows require hitting columns of size at least 3; only eight B vertices can host them, forcing at least five common B-neighbors for an A-edge, contradicting alpha(B)=4
proof_components.A0_edge_01: same common-neighbor obstruction, with cross needs 7 and 6
proof_components.A0_edges_05_06: all pair-supported 7-row starts die at independent-triple row support; only B1/B3/B8 have 6/4/2 pair-supported starts and all have zero triple-supported starts
proof_components.A0_other_edges: the degree-3 A vertex needs a triangle-free 8-row; B0..B3 have none and every 8-row in B4..B8 fails pair support with another required A row

conclusion: No m=220 R(4,6,36) graph can have exactly three degree-11 vertices.
